name: True/False (Binary Judgment)
summary: Statement displayed; select True or False. Ultra-fast decision cycle.

aiGenerability.notes: Trivial to generate. Create a true statement, then flip for false variant. Best when false statements are plausibly close to truth (e.g., 'Mars has 3 moons' vs. 'Mars has 2 moons'), not absurd.

statement.description: A declarative statement to be judged as true or false.

isTrue.description: Whether the statement is actually true (used for grading).

explanation.description: Brief explanation of the correct answer and why the statement is true or false.

difficulty.description: Difficulty level based on how obvious the answer is.

ux.mobileNotes: Two large side-by-side buttons (True | False) or stacked vertically on very small screens. Clear visual distinction between buttons. Large font (18-20pt) for statement text.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Bigger visual buttons (64x64px). True button green, False button red. Large icons (checkmark, X) in addition to text. Simple, unambiguous statements. No trick statements. Positive feedback tone.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Standard 56x56px buttons. Statements can be more nuanced. False statements should be plausibly close to truth. Constructive feedback explaining the trap.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Timed rapid-fire variant (5-8s per statement). Challenging statements requiring careful reading (e.g., 'Most of the Earth's oxygen is produced by trees' — False, it's ocean plankton). High-speed scoring with leaderboards.
